changes.detail: `perTenantConnectionCap` also takes a function of the tenant id, read on every `route()`, so one router can give a dev-mode site that loads dozens of modules at once a higher cap than an app that should never hold more than a few. A number works as before.

A connection to a host that vanished gets no refusal, so fetch hangs. After afterMs with no response headers, the gateway tries a TCP connection to the upstream. A slow app still accepts one and is left to answer. A failed connection stops the request as unreachable, so onUpstreamFailure and retry apply within seconds.
changes.summary: upstreamLiveness: tell a dead host from a slow one while a request waits
excludeShards: keep a route request off shards that already failed it

changes.detail: Only methods safe to repeat (GET, HEAD, OPTIONS) are retried, once by default, on a fresh route that excludes the shards already tried. onUpstreamFailure lets a caller stop routing to a dead shard before its next health check. upstreamHeadersTimeoutMs answers 504 and never retries, so slow work never runs twice.
changes.summary: The Bun gateway retries a request whose upstream cannot be reached on another shard, reports each failed upstream, and can bound how long an upstream takes to send its headers
preserveHost: send the client's Host to the upstream so apps behind the gateway see their public name
Pass compressed responses through the Bun gateway as the app encoded them

changes.detail: Set publicProtocol from trusted deployment settings when ingress terminates TLS. Forged client forwarding headers remain ignored.
changes.summary: Preserve the configured public HTTPS protocol through HTTP and WebSocket gateways behind TLS termination
